title: Sweeping Decision Thresholds for Precision, Recall, and F1
description: Evaluate (y_prob >= thr).astype(int) across the supplied thresholds from 0.0 to 1.0, print the first five (thr, p, r, f1) rows, and plot Precision vs. Recall.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Generate evenly spaced thresholds from 0.0 to 1.0 using the supplied count. Convert `y_prob` into binary predictions `y_hat = (y_prob >= thr).astype(int)` at each `thr`, and record `(thr, p, r, f1)` using `precision_recall_fscore_support`.
Loop over the first 5 tuples in `pairs[:5]` (`t=0.00` through `t=0.20`) and print `Precision`, `Recall`, and `F1`.

Look at line 5: raising `thr` requires a higher predicted probability `y_prob` before `y_hat` predicts `1`, which reduces false positives (`Precision` rises) while risking more false negatives (`Recall` eventually drops).

steps.question: At `thr = 0.00` on line 5, what does `(y_prob >= 0.0).astype(int)` predict for every test sample? What are `Recall` and `Precision`?
steps.answer: Every probability is `>= 0.0`, so `y_hat` is `1` for all samples. `Recall` is `1.000` (all actual positives found), and `Precision` is `0.629`.

steps.description: Convert `pairs` into the 2D array `pr = np.array(pairs)` and plot `pr[:, 1]` (`Precision`) against `pr[:, 2]` (`Recall`) across all thresholds.
